newsitem.title: JAPAN: DKB likely to name new president by Friday - paper.
newsitem.headline: DKB likely to name new president by Friday - paper.

text.p: Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd will probably announce a change in its top management before its board of directors' meeting on Friday, the Nihon Keizai Shimbun business daily said on Wednesday.

Nihon Keizai and other Japanese media reported that DKB chairman Tadashi Okuda and president Katsuhiko Kondo were expected to resign to take responsibility for DKB's involvement in a scandal at Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
Kuniji Miyazaki, who is currently an adviser to the bank but was president when, the reports said, the bank began making loans to a corporate racketeer in the 1980s, would also resign, they reported.
A DKB spokesman said that no such a decision had been made.
Media reports have linked DKB with corporate extortionist Ryuichi Koike, at the centre of the Nomura racketeer payoff scandal.
